reviews.body: > [!NOTE] > **Newer findings are available below.** Devin Review posted a newer report on this PR, in addition to the findings presented here. ## ✅ Devin Review: No Issues Found Devin Review analyzed this PR and found no bugs or issues to report.

Hi @pcbeingused333, thanks for this PR!

A heads-up on the changelog entry: this repository moved from `.changes/` to [verwalter](https://github.com/livekit/verwalter) changesets in #1311. The changeset check now looks for a file in `.changeset/` instead of `.changes/`.

Here is your entry in the new format, ready to copy:

`.changeset/reconnect-after-republish-failure.md`, in place of `.changes/reconnect-after-republish-failure`:

```md
---
livekit_client: patch
---

Complete room reconnection even when republishing local tracks fails
```

The `type=` kind is gone. The changelog adds the PR number and the author to the entry instead. You can also write the file with `verwalter changeset --level <level> --package livekit_client --summary "..."`.

Thanks again!
**Devin Review** found 2 new potential issues.

review_comments.body:
🟡 **False reconnection after room disconnect** If the room disconnects while republishing awaits an acknowledgment, `rePublishAllTracks()` can time out after the disconnect. The handler then emits `RoomReconnectedEvent` for a room that is no longer connected.
Learn more A full restart emits [EngineRestartedEvent](https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-flutter/blob/fd919999630153f43997ad8ef297ec563540c67a/lib/src/core/engine.dart#L1400-L1417 "lib/src/core/engine.dart:1400-1417") before the room finishes restoring local media. Restoring a microphone publication calls [addTrack](https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-flutter/blob/fd919999630153f43997ad8ef297ec563540c67a/lib/src/participant/local.dart#L208-L214 "lib/src/participant/local.dart:208-214"), whose [acknowledgment wait](https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-flutter/blob/fd919999630153f43997ad8ef297ec563540c67a/lib/src/core/engine.dart#L378-L387 "lib/src/core/engine.dart:378-387") throws on timeout. An app can call [disconnect](https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-flutter/blob/fd919999630153f43997ad8ef297ec563540c67a/lib/src/core/room.dart#L789-L801 "lib/src/core/room.dart:789-801") during that wait, as the [disconnect control](https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-flutter/blob/fd919999630153f43997ad8ef297ec563540c67a/example/lib/widgets/controls.dart#L227-L230 "example/lib/widgets/controls.dart:227-230") does. Once [signal cleanup](https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-flutter/blob/fd919999630153f43997ad8ef297ec563540c67a/lib/src/core/signal_client.dart#L241-L249 "lib/src/core/signal_client.dart:241-249") closes the socket, the outstanding request no longer receives its acknowledgment. The new catch allows the stale handler to reach [the completion event](https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-flutter/blob/fd919999630153f43997ad8ef297ec563540c67a/lib/src/core/room.dart#L641-L649 "lib/src/core/room.dart:641-649") even after the disconnect. **Example:** The SDK rejoins a room and sends an add-track request for the microphone. The user hangs up before the response arrives and the server closes the session. The publish wait expires and the app receives a reconnection success event despite the completed hangup. **Recommended fix:** After the republish await, verify that the engine still owns the active reconnect session before restoring settings or announcing success. At minimum, reject a closed engine or a room that is no longer connected. Add a regression that disconnects before the republish wait settles and asserts that no later success event fires.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Missing reconnect fix in changelog** When generating a release, [parseChanges](https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-flutter/blob/fd919999630153f43997ad8ef297ec563540c67a/scripts/create_version.dart#L155-L180 "scripts/create_version.dart:155-180") ignores this patch entry because it only scans `.changes/`. The generated changelog omits the reconnect fix.
Learn more The [release rules](https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-flutter/blob/fd919999630153f43997ad8ef297ec563540c67a/AGENTS.md "AGENTS.md") require one line in `.changes/` for published changes. The release generator does not scan the directory used by this PR, and moving the file without converting its contents would fail the parser. **Example:** A release containing this PR includes other patch entries but omits the fix for reconnecting after a local track fails to republish. **Recommended fix:** Replace the Markdown file with `.changes/reconnect-after-republish-failure` containing `patch type="fixed" "Complete room reconnection even when republishing local tracks fails"`.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

comments.body:
Real-device data for this, in case it helps review. No server kill needed: an ordinary network drop reaches the same path.

**Setup:** `livekit_client` 2.13.2, `flutter_webrtc` 1.6.3, local `livekit-server` in Docker. Full reconnect triggered by switching Wi-Fi off for 5 s and back on. Track state read with `ListParticipants` 12 s after the client was back in the room.

**Xiaomi POCO F1, Android 10, 10 Wi-Fi drops per condition:**

| Mic before the drop | `addTransceiver(): track is null` (unhandled) | Mic track after reconnect |
|---|---|---|
| live | 0/10 | live 10/10 |
| muted (`setMicrophoneEnabled(false)`) | 1/10 | muted 5/10, **not published** 5/10 |

Motorola g96, Android 15: the same unhandled exception on 2 of 5 Wi-Fi-off / airplane-mode reconnects (mic state not recorded).

Same stack as the issue (`_publishAudioTrack.negotiate` → `rePublishAllTracks` → `EngineRestartedEvent` handler), and it matches the muted-mic condition described there.

Two notes:
- Catching here fixes what hurts most in production: the error is unhandled (in our app, which reports unhandled errors through `PlatformDispatcher.onError`, it shows up as a **fatal** crash), and `RoomReconnectedEvent` never fires.
- In 5 of 10 muted runs the mic track was not republished at all, **with no exception logged**, so that looks like a separate path from the one this PR catches. Unmuting afterwards published the mic normally.

Thanks for the detailed real-device numbers, @ashwinrj2255-coder. This confirms the muted-mic condition and that the `addTransceiver(): track is null` error is reachable through an ordinary Wi-Fi drop, which is the path this PR now catches so that the reconnect completes and `RoomReconnectedEvent` fires.

The 5/10 muted runs where the mic is not republished and no exception is logged look like a separate path from the one fixed here, so I'd keep it out of this PR and look at it separately. If it would help, could you open an issue with the logs from one of those runs?

Follow-up on my earlier numbers: I re-ran this on the same POCO F1 (Android 10, livekit_client 2.13.2, local livekit-server 1.13.11), mic muted before a 5 s Wi-Fi drop, this time with SDK logging at `ALL` and logcat streamed for the whole run instead of read afterwards.

10 runs: 8 went through a full reconnect, and all 8 threw `addTransceiver(): track is null` from `rePublishAllTracks` and ended with no mic publication. The other 2 resumed the session (no full reconnect), kept the muted mic published and threw nothing.

So the earlier "not published, no exception" runs don't hold up. With complete logs, every lost mic coincides with this exception. The earlier harness read `logcat -d` after the run, and the line most likely rotated out of the buffer. There's no separate path to report. Sorry for the noise.

Note that with this PR the reconnect completes, but the muted mic still ends up unpublished (the `track.start()` point in #1274), since the stopped track's `mediaStreamTrack` isn't recreated before `addTransceiver`.

Thanks for re-running this with full logcat, @ashwinrj2255-coder. That settles it: all 8 full reconnects hit `addTransceiver(): track is null`, so there is no separate path, and no need to apologise for the earlier numbers.

Agreed on the remaining part: with this PR the reconnect completes and `RoomReconnectedEvent` fires, while the muted mic staying unpublished comes from the stopped track not being recreated before `addTransceiver` (the `track.start()` point in #1274). I'll keep that out of this PR so it stays scoped to the exception.
